samples.summary: New invariant "an app-issued redirect must be a `replace`" is declared but nothing enforces it
samples.evidence: sync-status.md:314-321 elevates "an app-issued redirect is a `replace`" from an observation to "an **invariant this app has to uphold**", and the fix implements it by hand-editing the two `<Navigate>` call sites (PrivateRoute.tsx:36, PublicRoute.tsx:24). Because `<Navigate>` defaults to `replace={false}`, any future app-issued redirect written as `<Navigate to=... />` silently routes through the guard — exactly the case the doc says the guard cannot answer (a *Stay* on an expired session strands the user). I found no lint rule, no test, and no wrapper component that would catch the regression: the guard provider itself cannot distinguish an app redirect from a user push, and knip/eslint/vitest lanes have no rule for `<Navigate>`. An alternative approach fit (a small `<Redirect>` wrapper, or a lint rule requiring `replace` on `<Navigate>`) would make the invariant structural rather than a convention every future author has to remember. Cost stays inside the codebase today — all 8 current `<Navigate>` sites do pass `replace` — so this is minor, not major.

samples.summary: Auth-routing components now carry comments explaining a sync-status subsystem's internals
samples.evidence: PublicRoute.tsx:21-23 and PrivateRoute.tsx:32-35 explain their `replace` in terms of `NavigationGuardProvider` ("holds back pushes only"). That couples the auth-routing layer's inline documentation to the sync-status guard's implementation detail, which the design doc already records at docs/design/sync-status.md:314. A one-line "redirect, not a push" plus the existing doc pointer would keep the rationale in one place and avoid two comments that must be updated together if the guard's push/replace split ever changes.
